figures.finding: Czech actors' union is the Herecká asociace (HA), an independent professional and trade-union organisation of performers founded in 1994; one joins by the online application and an entry fee of CZK 250 (CZK 40 for pensioners and students), then dues of CZK 150 a month for theatre only or audiovisual only, CZK 300 for both, CZK 200 a year for students, pensioners and parents on maternity leave. Membership is not stated as a condition of engagement.
figures.applies: Czech Republic, performers; fees as published 2026-11-01.

figures.finding: An actor employed by a public theatre (a contributory organisation of the state, a region or a town) is paid a monthly tariff by the pay class the work catalogue gives the work: class 10 for interpreting roles, 11 for lead or demanding roles, 12 for the most demanding roles and 13 for the most demanding roles at the highest nationally recognised level. The regulation's scale steps each class by years of practice, and an employer may set an artist's tariff anywhere between the class's lowest and highest step by its collective agreement or internal rule (§ 6), so a class's lowest step (CZK 27,030, 29,090, 31,230 and 33,590 a month in the version in force from 1 April 2026) is the least a public theatre may pay.

value.regulation: Nařízení vlády č. 341/2017 Sb., příloha č. 1, with § 6 (1) (b); Nařízení vlády č. 222/2010 Sb., 2.14.08

classes.13: the most demanding roles at the highest nationally recognised level

figures.applies: Czechia, actors employed by public theatres from 1 April 2026; private theatres and freelance engagements are set by contract, and film and television have no minimum found.
